header:
Date: 2025-05-13
Start: 10:30 AM PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Sofia Ramirez (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (HelixAI ML Eng), Jordan Lee (HelixAI CTO), Alex Chen (HelixAI SRE), Priya Nair (HelixAI Data Scientist)
Recording: yes
Artifacts shared: quant-bench-2025-05-13.xlsx (Redwood), slides: quantiz-qa.pdf
summary: Weekly POC sync to review INT8/FP8 quantization experiments. Redwood presented updated perf deltas (throughput, p99 latency, GPU memory) and quality metrics on prompt test sets. Conversation covered calibration approaches, per-layer sensitivity, KV cache implications, and rollback/fallback strategies. HelixAI to run 24h INT8 pilot with provided configs; Redwood to share detailed logs and per-layer histograms. Planned deep dive next week if regressions persist.
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do a quick recap then go into the quant results.
[00:14] Jordan: sounds good. we have limited time but want to see the perf numbers and any quality regressions.
[00:26] Sofia: Great. Ethan, can you kick off with the INT8 vs FP8 slide?
[00:34] Ethan: yeah, sure. so slide one, apologies if the slide numbers are off, um we ran the model - your 7B variant - across three configs: baseline FP16, INT8 with per-layer calibration, and experimental FP8. the headline: INT8 gives ~1.9-2.3x throughput improvement and reduces memory by about 30-35% depending on sequence length, FP8 is closer to 2.5x but with slightly higher variance on some prompts.
[01:05] Priya: when you say variance, is that variance in latency or in output quality?
[01:11] Ethan: primarily output quality on a small subset of the prompt set \u0004 we observed 0.8 to 1.5 point delta on our rouge/qa style metrics for a handful of prompts, some hallucination cases increased. latency variance is small but p99 for FP8 sometimes spikes on long sequences.
[01:31] Maya: can you show the exact examples where QA dropped? we flagged a few in the leaderboard.
[01:36] Ethan: yep, pull up the examples. [00:00: pauses, shuffling] Example A \u0004 prompt about financial reconciliation \u0004 FP16 and INT8 returned similar answer, FP8 truncated a step and added an extra clause that wasn't asked for, likely due to quant noise in attention matrix.
[02:05] Alex: that aligns with what we worried about around attention head sensitivity. did you test per-head quant scaling?
[02:12] Ethan: we tried per-layer scaling first, per-head is on the roadmap but increases calibration complexity and run-time overhead. initial tests show per-head can reduce those hallucination cases but not without extra memory for scaling factors.
[02:28] Jordan: what's the calibration time look like for INT8? we don't want a huge offline step.
[02:33] Ethan: calibration on a 10k sample took about 45 minutes on a single A100 in our environment, it's not enormous. calibration can be incremental too \u0004 you can run a smaller sample and refine.
[02:47] Priya: any special considerations for KV cache and quantization? our production workload is decoder-only with long chat history.
[02:55] Ethan: good point. KV cache values are stored in quantized form for INT8 path, we maintain dequant steps on response. For long histories, INT8 reduces memory footprint but we've seen slightly higher token generation time when cache hits are frequent because of dequant overhead; overall throughput still improved but p99 latency can be impacted.
[03:18] Maya: hmm, for chat SLOs p99 is important. do you have numbers for tokens/sec vs p99 delta for 1k-2k sequence lengths?
[03:26] Ethan: yes, for 1k seq INT8 tokens/sec went up ~2.1x, p50 latency dropped similarly, p99 improved by ~10-15% in most runs but in a few runs it spiked because of cache decompress contention. we'll share the raw perf logs.
[03:46] Sofia: quick interjection \u0004 we also tested a hybrid: keep KV cache in FP16 and quantize only weights for INT8. that reduces p99 spikes but loses some memory savings. a trade-off to consider.
[04:00] Jordan: what's our recommended path for the POC then? full INT8 or hybrid?
[04:06] Ethan: recommend hybrid as a low-risk first step for chat-heavy workloads. run INT8 for weights, keep KV cache in FP16, run per-layer calibration, monitor quality regressions, then move to full INT8 if results are stable.
[04:20] Priya: what about fallback strategies if we detect a regression? automatic route to FP16?
[04:26] Ethan: yes, we have runtime fallback \u0004 route requests that fail heuristics to FP16 model or to a safer model variant. Redwood's routing can do A/B or canary rollouts per user segment.
[04:40] Maya: can you quantify the false negative rate for the heuristics? we don't want to flip too often.
[04:46] Ethan: heuristics are conservative; initial tuning gives fallback rates <2% on our workloads, but that'll vary by prompt set. we recommend a short warmup with heavy monitoring.
[04:58] Jordan: how about the quality metrics \u0004 you mentioned rouge/qa. can we integrate our own evals?
[05:04] Sofia: absolutely \u0004 we can run your eval harness against the quantized variants and produce regression alerts. that's part of Redwood Optimize pipeline.
[05:13] Priya: one more question: FP8 - are we using a block FP8 or channel-wise? what's the format?
[05:20] Ethan: the FP8 run used experimental block FP8 with shared exponent per block, that's why we see higher variance on edge prompts. per-channel FP8 is more stable but costlier to implement and less supported on some runtimes.
[05:33] Alex: any infra changes for Dedicated vs Hosted? we plan to start on Hosted then move to Dedicated if we see consistent numbers.
[05:41] Ethan: Hosted supports all quant paths; Dedicated gives you more control over kernel selection and pinning GPU types which can squeeze more perf out of INT8/FP8. If you move to Dedicated, we can provide a tuned deployment with specific kernels and batch configs.
[05:58] Maya: can we see the exact commands or runtime flags to reproduce your runs?
[06:03] Ethan: yes, we'll push a reproducibility script and the docker run flags. expect it in the spreadsheet.
[06:10] Sofia: ok quick recap of the perf deltas we showed: INT8 ~2x tokens/sec, FP8 ~2.4-2.7x but with higher variance; memory savings INT8 30-35%, FP8 up to 40%. quality: small regressions on a small subset, FP8 slightly worse on hallucinations.
[06:32] Jordan: acceptable if we can route risky traffic away. what's your suggested monitoring to catch regressions live?
[06:39] Ethan: monitor per-prompt log-likelihood delta, entropy, and a small set of sentinel prompts (the prod equivalent of canary prompts). combine that with output-difference detectors (n-gram overlap drops) and human review samples.
[06:55] Priya: can we push log-likelihoods into our existing observability stack (Datadog)?
[07:00] Ethan: yes, Redwood can emit metrics to Datadog, and we can add trace hooks.
[07:05] Maya: scheduling: we said HelixAI will run a 24h pilot on INT8. what's the expected artifact?
[07:10] Sofia: logs, per-request latencies, a sample of outputs for the failing prompts, and the calibration config used.
[07:16] Maya: ok we'll do that.
[07:18] Alex: one ops question: what's the rollback time if we detect problems?
[07:22] Ethan: with routing rules you can flip back in under a minute at the control plane level, but draining in-flight requests may add a little time. plan for a minute to a few minutes.
[07:34] Jordan: any compliance/security concerns with quantized models? you're not sending any extra telemetry right?
[07:39] Sofia: no, same telemetry as baseline; encryption and KMS handling unchanged. we keep calibration artifacts local to your Dedicated environment if needed.
[07:50] Priya: do we need SOC 2 addendum for the pilot?
[07:53] Sofia: our standard SOC 2 attestation covers hosted; if you need a specific addendum for Dedicated we'll loop legal \u0004 but for pilot hosted it's usually fine.
[08:03] Maya: great. last item\u0001pricing impact. Sofia?
[08:07] Sofia: we estimated cost savings per-token at around 25-35% for INT8 vs FP16, FP8 slightly higher but it's variable. I'll send an updated pricing worksheet accounting for Dedicated commit scenarios as well.
[08:21] Jordan: that's helpful. any risks we haven't covered?
[08:25] Ethan: model-specific sensitivity is the big unknown \u0004 some models are more robust to low-precision. per-layer calibration and sentinel prompts mitigate but not eliminate. per-head quant is a follow-up if needed.
[08:38] Maya: ok let's lock next steps.
[08:40] Sofia: next steps: we'll send spreadsheet and reproducibility scripts; Ethan will share layer histograms; Maya to run 24h INT8 pilot; reconvene next Tuesday for deep dive if any regressions.
[08:52] Jordan: good, thanks everyone.
[08:55] Priya: thanks.
[08:56] Sofia: thanks all, meeting adjourned.
notes: Redwood recommends hybrid INT8 (weights) + FP16 KV cache for chat-first workloads as low-risk path
FP8 gives higher theoretical speedups but exhibits more variance in output quality on a small subset of prompts
Calibration cost modest; per-head quant reduces some regressions but adds complexity
Fallback/routing and sentinel prompt monitoring are essential for safe rollout
